Subject: Three-way renewal financing & seat-swap options

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the candid conversation earlier. Per our notes, Pillara is looking to: (1) expand committed capacity mid-contract, (2) co-term the new capacity with your existing renewal window, and (3) avoid a large one-time invoice to keep quarterly budgets smooth.

I attached a short outline (Pillara_Renewal_Outline_v1.pdf) that lays out three paths we can run in parallel: a straightforward top-up + pro-rated invoice; a staged ramp with amortized payments across the remaining contract months; or a three-way financing split where software spend is distributed across two cost centers (AI platform + product research) and we provide a small bridge credit in month 1.

Can you confirm which of the three you want us to model (Top-up | Staged Ramp | 3-way split)? If it's the three-way split, please share the billing contacts for both cost centers and any PO timing constraints.

I’ve looped Lauren for legal/PO timing and Ben for pricing scenarios. If helpful we can run a 30-minute pricing walk-through tomorrow.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Subject: RE: Three-way renewal financing & seat-swap options — pricing scenarios

Jonas / team —

Per Maria’s asks I modeled three discrete scenarios (high level):

1) Top-up (Immediate + Pro-rate)
- +40% committed units effective 2026-10-01
- One-time pro-rated invoice for remainder of current contract quarter: $72,000 (net)
- No consolidation discount applied

2) Staged Ramp (3-month amortized top-up)
- +40% committed units phased: Oct 1 (+20%), Nov 1 (+30%), Dec 1 (+40%)
- Monthly amortized invoices: Oct $28,000 / Nov $34,000 / Dec $38,000
- Total over 3 months equals $100,000 gross, with a 4% service credit if staged payments accepted by 10/15

3) Three-way split (finance-friendly) — recommended for procurement
- Redwood issues a bridge invoice in Oct for 30% of uplift, Pillara allocates across CostCenter-A (AI platform) and CostCenter-B (Product Research) per provided percentages
- Remaining 70% amortized across remaining contract months through 2027-03-31 (co-term)
- If Pillara agrees to co-term 2027-03-31 we can extend a 6% consolidation discount on the uplift portion (requires signed amendment)
- Estimated net monthly impact after split & discount: $12,500/month (example allocation 60/40)

Notes / dependencies:
- Any consolidation discount requires a legal amendment and PO to lock the co-term window — looping Lauren for timing.
- Bridge credit is limited to 10% of uplift and structured as a one-time account credit applied to the Oct invoice.
- I attached a simplified ledger (SOW-Draft_PillarA.docx) with line items to drop into procurement.

If that aligns I can prepare a one-page amendment and a month-by-month invoice table to send to procurement.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: SOW-Draft_PillarA.docx (DOCX, 28KB)

Subject: RE: Three-way renewal financing & seat-swap options

Maria / Procurement —

Thanks — Ben’s scenarios are the three we typically use. I attached the month-by-month invoice impact for the three-way split with an example 60/40 allocation (CostCenter-A / CostCenter-B) and the proposed amendment language to co-term to 2027-03-31. Summary below: 

- Oct 2026: Bridge invoice (30% uplift) — $30,000 gross, credit applied: $3,000 (bridge credit) => $27,000 net
- Nov–Mar (5 months): $12,500/month (amortized remainder after allocation & discount)
- Co-term consolidation discount (6%) applies only if amendment and PO are signed by 2026-09-20

Action items for Pillara:
- Confirm allocation percentages for the two cost centers (example used 60/40)
- Confirm procurement PO timing and whether the PO will reference the co-term amendment
- If yes to both, we can lock the 6% consolidation discount and issue an updated invoice schedule by EOD Wednesday.

Would you like Ben and I on the Wed 10am PT call? We can walk procurement through the ledger and amendment.

Best,
Jonas
